papers.title: EINN: An enzyme-informed neural network guided by an enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic model.
papers.abstract: Predicting cellular metabolism from molecular data is a central challenge in systems biology, with direct implications for engineering microbial cell factories. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) provide a mechanistic foundation for such predictions, but their accuracy is limited by an inability to account for the finite catalytic capacity of the proteome. Enzyme-constrained GEMs (ecGEMs) address this by incorporating enzyme turnover numbers and proteome allocation constraints. Hybrid neural-mechanistic models like Artificial Metabolic Network (AMN) and Metabolic-Informed Neural Network (MIN
papers.summary: This paper introduces EINN, a hybrid neural network that integrates an enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic model (ecGEM) to predict cellular metabolism more accurately than standard mechanistic or purely data-driven approaches. By incorporating enzyme turnover numbers and proteome allocation constraints, EINN improves predictions of metabolic fluxes and phenotypes, offering a valuable tool for engineering microbial cell factories.

papers.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. The active transcriptome, encompassi
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.summary: This study integrates deep learning-based genome annotation, multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network inference to characterize the roles of aquaporins, heat shock proteins, and LEA proteins in the halophyte Portulaca oleracea under salt stress. It identifies 78 AQPs, 525 HSPs, and 119 LEA proteins and reveals their coordinated transcriptional regulation, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms of salt tolerance.

papers.title: Molecular Systems Architecture of Fibrotic Lung Microenvironment in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Background: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible fibrosing interstitial lung disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, disruption of lung architecture, and progressive loss of pulmonary function. IPF is frequently accompanied by comorbid conditions that exacerbate disease progression and negatively impact prognosis. To address the biological complexity of IPF, this study presents a comprehensive molecular systems architecture that enables a system-level understanding of biomolecular interactions within the fibrotic lung microen
papers.summary: This study presents a comprehensive molecular systems architecture of the fibrotic lung microenvironment in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), integrating multi-omics data to map biomolecular interactions. The findings provide a system-level understanding of the disease, potentially revealing new therapeutic targets and biomarkers.

papers.title: FERRET: Framework to Evaluate Robustness in Regulatory Networks Using Heterogeneous Cell Types.
papers.abstract: Techniques for evaluating gene regulatory network (GRN) inference methods typically focus on recovering small ground-truth networks or on benchmarking against simulated data. However, both approaches have important limitations and fail to capture the biological variability present in real datasets. FERRET is a framework for benchmarking single-cell GRN inference methods based on a simple biological assumption: independent estimates of the regulatory network from the same cellular state should resemble one another more closely than estimates from distinct cellular states. Rather than relying on
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FERRET is a new benchmarking framework for single-cell gene regulatory network (GRN) inference methods that evaluates robustness by comparing network estimates from the same versus different cellular states, rather than relying on simulated or small ground-truth networks. This approach better captures biological variability in real datasets and provides a more realistic assessment of GRN inference performance.

papers.title: Residual-stream geometry of single-cell foundation models carries incremental gene-regulatory signal across tissues.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT and Geneformer learn rich representations of gene expression programs, but whether these representations encode gene regulatory relationships beyond expression-level confounds remains unclear. Attention patterns in these models have been shown to capture co-expression rather than direct regulation, leaving open the question of whether deeper representations-particularly the residual stream-contain genuine regulatory information.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether single-cell foundation models like scGPT and Geneformer encode gene regulatory information beyond mere co-expression. The authors find that the residual-stream representations of these models carry incremental gene-regulatory signal across tissues, suggesting that deeper layers contain genuine regulatory information not captured by attention patterns alone.

papers.title: SignifiKANTE: Efficient P-value computation for gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are graph-based representations of regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes. Various tools exist to infer GRNs from gene expression data, but since GRN inference itself is already computationally intensive, statistical significance estimates are often omitted. While naïve permutation-based empirical P-value computation methods are relatively straightforward to implement, they are prohibitively expensive when applied to popular regression-based GRN inference methods and realistically sized datasets.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SignifiKANTE, a tool that efficiently computes empirical P-values for gene regulatory network inference, addressing the computational bottleneck that often leads to omitted significance estimates. It enables practical statistical significance testing for regression-based GRN methods on realistic datasets.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of single-cell foundation model interpretability: attention-derived edge scores add no incremental value over gene-level features for perturbation-target prediction.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT and Geneformer are increasingly used for gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, with attention-derived edge scores routinely interpreted as regulatory proxies. Prior benchmarks have evaluated curated-reference recovery but have not systematically tested whether attention adds information beyond expression statistics for predicting the outcomes of genetic perturbations, nor whether attention-identified "regulatory" components are causally required for such predictions. This gap matters because the NLP interpretability literature has established that
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates whether attention-derived edge scores from single-cell foundation models like scGPT and Geneformer provide additional predictive value for perturbation outcomes beyond simple gene-level expression features. The authors find that attention-based edge scores add no incremental information, suggesting that these interpretability signals may not be causally meaningful for regulatory inference.

papers.title: Systems-Level Mapping of the Tumor Microenvironment Reveals Immune-Mediated Mechanisms and Potential Targets in Platinum-Resistant Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic cancer, with limited improvements in patient survival despite targeted therapies and a high recurrence rate (~80%). Current standard-of-care for frontline treatment involves platinum-based chemotherapy, but the emergence of resistant clones limits long-term efficacy. Existing models often overlook critical interactions between cancer cells and their microenvironment. Therefore, we investigated the ovarian cancer microenvironment to identify cell populations and markers driving treatment resistance.
papers.summary: This study maps the tumor microenvironment of platinum-resistant ovarian cancer at a systems level, identifying immune cell populations and markers that drive treatment resistance. The findings reveal immune-mediated mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets, offering new insights beyond cancer-cell-intrinsic factors.

papers.title: Loss of ATP-Dependent Citrate Lyase Drives Left Ventricular Dysfunction by Metabolic Remodeling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic adaptation and maladaptation are hallmarks of the failing heart and may be a target for therapeutic interventions. For example, sustained glucose oxidation during cardiac stress is associated with increased activity and abundance of ACL (ATP-dependent citrate lyase, Acly), which produces acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) from citrate and CoA and supports de novo lipid synthesis. However, our understanding of how ACL supports cardiac metabolic adaptation and its potential to modulate disease pathophysiology has not yet been investigated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of ATP-dependent citrate lyase (ACL) in cardiac metabolic adaptation and heart failure. The authors find that loss of ACL drives left ventricular dysfunction through metabolic remodeling, suggesting that ACL may be a therapeutic target for heart failure.

papers.title: Systemic trade-offs between core and accessory genomes govern stress adaptation in Rhodococcus erythropolis.
papers.abstract: The genus Rhodococcus is a premier biotechnological chassis for organic pollutant bioremediation and natural product biosynthesis, yet the systemic genetic basis of its stress resilience remains poorly defined. Here, we elucidate adaptive strategies in Rhodococcus erythropolis by integrating pangenomics with multi-omics and phenotypic analyses. We refined R. erythropolis taxonomy using average nucleotide identity across 671 genomes and constructed a high-quality pangenome that exhibits an open architecture, with continuous expansion of the accessory cloud genome via horizontal gene transfer to
papers.summary: This study integrates pangenomics with multi-omics and phenotypic analyses to reveal how Rhodococcus erythropolis balances core and accessory genomes for stress adaptation, showing that the accessory genome expands through horizontal gene transfer and drives niche-specific resilience. The findings provide a systemic view of the genetic basis of stress tolerance in this biotechnologically important bacterium.

papers.title: Hormone-metabolism crosstalk in plants: an integrated signaling network coordinating growth and stress adaptation.
papers.abstract: Plant growth, stress adaptation, and productivity depend on the continuous exchange of information between hormone signaling and metabolic networks. Although major phytohormones have been widely studied through their biosynthesis, receptors, and downstream transcriptional modules, these pathways are still often presented as linear systems. This view does not fully explain how plants integrate carbon status, nutrient availability, redox balance, cellular energy, and developmental signals under changing environments. In this review, we present plant hormone signaling and metabolism as a reciproc
papers.summary: This review argues that plant hormone signaling and metabolism should be viewed as an integrated, reciprocal network rather than linear pathways, highlighting how carbon status, nutrients, redox balance, and energy signals coordinate growth and stress responses. It synthesizes current knowledge to propose a more holistic framework for understanding plant adaptation.

papers.title: Latent gene network expression underlies partial re-evolution of a polyphenic trait in the worker caste of ants.
papers.abstract: Polyphenisms-where alternative phenotypes develop from a single genome in response to environmental cues-are not only widespread in nature, but also occur at multiple levels of biological organization, from cells to individuals to societies. Polyphenism is thought to promote phenotypic diversification through the gain, loss, and re-evolution of alternative phenotypes. After the origin of a polyphenism, one of the alternative phenotypes often retains the developmental capacity to produce the ancestral trait, thereby permitting the other to evolve rapidly. Yet, little is known about the developm
papers.summary: This study investigates how a polyphenic trait in ants—the worker caste's ability to produce soldiers—was partially re-evolved after its loss. The authors find that latent gene network expression, rather than new mutations, underlies this re-evolution, suggesting that ancestral developmental capacity can be retained and reactivated. This provides insight into the mechanisms of phenotypic re-evolution and polyphenism.

papers.title: A fungal exudate-inspired substrate mixture elicits an emergent growth phenotype and metabolic responses in Pseudomonas putida.
papers.abstract: Microbes in natural environments often encounter diverse mixtures of organic compounds, yet how mixed substrate environments and their molecular composition shape microbial phenotypes remains understudied. Here, we examined how a defined fungal exudate mimic (FEM) mixture influences growth and metabolism in Pseudomonas putida KT2440 compared to individual substrates matched for total carbon and nitrogen. Growth on FEM initiated 2 h earlier than growth on glucose alone and exhibited both the lowest lag and shortest time to maximum biomass compared to individual substrates. Fructose was the only
papers.summary: This study shows that a defined mixture of compounds mimicking fungal exudates triggers earlier and faster growth in Pseudomonas putida compared to individual substrates, even when total carbon and nitrogen are matched. The findings highlight that substrate diversity itself, not just nutrient quantity, can shape microbial phenotypes and metabolic responses.

papers.title: A metabolic model of the leaf-associated bacterium Paraburkholderia dioscoreae links the ethylene precursor ACC to core carbon pathways.
papers.abstract: Paraburkholderia dioscoreae MSB3T is a novel species with potential agricultural impact, isolated from leaf acumens of the "air potato yam" Dioscorea bulbifera. P. dioscoreae's genome encodes a relevant combination of features mediating a beneficial plant-associated lifestyle, and it exhibits significant growth promotion when applied to agriculturally important plants such as tomato. Here, we constructed iPR1691, the first genome-scale metabolic model for P. dioscoreae MSB3, which includes 1,687 reactions, 1,487 metabolites, and 1,691 genes. From an available annotation of P. dioscoreae's geno
papers.summary: This study presents iPR1691, the first genome-scale metabolic model for the plant-associated bacterium Paraburkholderia dioscoreae, which links the ethylene precursor ACC to core carbon metabolism. The model provides a new resource for understanding how this bacterium promotes plant growth and may guide future agricultural applications.

papers.title: IAN, an intelligent system for omics data analysis and discovery.
papers.abstract: IAN is an R package addressing the challenge of integrating, analyzing, and interpreting gene expression data using an artificial intelligence (AI) system. It leverages popular pathway (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, and GO) and regulatory datasets (ChEA), along with STRING for protein-protein interactions, to perform standard enrichment analysis. A multi-agent architecture uses individual enrichment results to generate summaries using large language models (LLMs). These summaries are contextually integrated and interpreted by the LLM, guided by engineered prompts and grounding instructions, to
papers.summary: IAN is an R package that integrates gene expression data with pathway and regulatory databases, using a multi-agent AI system with large language models to generate contextual summaries and interpretations of enrichment results. It provides a user-friendly tool for omics data analysis and discovery.

papers.title: SBML level 3 package: flux balance constraints version 3.
papers.abstract: Constraint-based modeling is a well-established modeling methodology used to study biological networks at both the medium-scale and genome-scale. Due to their large size and complexity, such steady-state flux models are typically analyzed using constraint-based optimization techniques, such as Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). The Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) Package extends SBML Level 3 to provide a standardized format for encoding, exchanging, and annotating constraint-based models. It includes support for modeling concepts such as objective functions, flux bounds, and annotation of model compo
papers.summary: This paper describes version 3 of the Flux Balance Constraints (FBC) package for SBML Level 3, which provides a standardized format for encoding, exchanging, and annotating constraint-based models like those used in Flux Balance Analysis (FBA). The package supports key modeling concepts such as objective functions, flux bounds, and component annotations, facilitating interoperability and reproducibility in constraint-based modeling.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review highlights the emerging role of TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease, emphasizing how macrophage heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity contribute to disease progression. It positions TREM2 as a key molecular hub in immune-metabolic crosstalk and discusses its potential as a therapeutic target, while acknowledging the importance of timing in intervention.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome influences drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model identifies synergistic drug combinations in the presence of specific microbes like Fusobacterium nucleatum, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware therapy design.

papers.title: Integrative machine learning and single-nucleus transcriptomics reveal MAPK-centered neuronal responses underlying the potential Alzheimer's disease risk of GenX.
papers.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide-dimer acid (GenX or HFPO-DA) is a novel per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance developed as a replacement for legacy compounds, yet its potential neurotoxic effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we combined bibliometric profiling, in silico target prediction, in vivo behavioral assessments, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), network biology, machine learning, molecular docking, and in vitro validation to explore the potential relevance of GenX in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Bibliometric analysis revealed increasing research attention to GenX-associated he
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple approaches—including single-nucleus RNA sequencing, machine learning, and molecular docking—to investigate the neurotoxic effects of the PFAS replacement chemical GenX and its potential link to Alzheimer's disease. The findings reveal MAPK-centered neuronal responses that may underlie GenX-associated AD risk, providing a multi-omics framework for assessing environmental chemical neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Longitudinal zone- and cell type-specific pattern-triggered immune responses in Arabidopsis roots.
papers.abstract: Roots, composed of diverse cell types across longitudinal developmental zones, are vital for plant survival against microbial challenges. Leveraging single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging of Arabidopsis roots, we reveal here that plant-derived phytocytokines elicit more potent immune responses than microbe-derived patterns across root cell types and zones. The differential expression of receptors and key signaling modules in distinct cell types and zones contributes to the response intensity to specific elicitors. Phytocytokines sustain growth-defense trade-offs by suppressing the e
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging to map pattern-triggered immune responses across cell types and developmental zones in Arabidopsis roots. It finds that plant-derived phytocytokines trigger stronger immune responses than microbe-derived patterns, with receptor expression differences explaining the variation. The work reveals how roots balance growth and defense, providing a high-resolution view of root immunity.

papers.title: Deciphering cell state transitions by logical modeling with single-cell transcriptome data.
papers.abstract: Cell state transitions are essential for diverse cell fate decision processes. Such transitions are mostly irreversible in natural environments, but they can be reversed under certain conditions. This raises a question on the largely unknown regulatory mechanisms underlying the asymmetric cell state transitions in forward and backward directions. Here, we present scDECIPHER (single-cell dynamic explorer of complex interactions and pathway hierarchies), an integrative framework designed to address this question using single-cell resolution transcriptome data measured over cell state transitions
papers.summary: The authors introduce scDECIPHER, a computational framework that uses single-cell transcriptome data to model and understand the regulatory mechanisms driving cell state transitions, particularly focusing on why these transitions are often irreversible in one direction but can be reversed under specific conditions. This integrative approach aims to decipher the complex gene regulatory logic underlying asymmetric forward and backward cell state transitions.

papers.title: From one genome to thousands, and beyond.
papers.abstract: Over the past three decades, Saccharomyces cerevisiae has gone from being the first eukaryote to have its genome fully sequenced to one of the most studied biological systems. Advances in sequencing technologies, functional genomics, and population genomics have expanded the scope of study from a single laboratory reference genome to thousands of natural isolates, and the species-wide pangenome. These advances have revealed vast genetic and structural diversity, shaped by evolution, ecology, and domestication, while large-scale experimental resources have made yeast a model organism of choice
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of Saccharomyces cerevisiae research from the first eukaryotic genome sequence to a species-wide pangenome, highlighting how advances in sequencing and functional genomics have revealed vast genetic diversity shaped by evolution and domestication. It underscores yeast's role as a premier model organism for large-scale experimental studies.

papers.title: Biochemical principles of SMAD signaling across the animal kingdom.
papers.abstract: The bone-morphogenetic protein (BMP)-SMAD signal transduction pathway regulates fundamental cellular processes such as fate specification, tissue patterning, and stem cell homeostasis across metazoans and has a conserved signaling architecture. However, the quantitative dynamics of SMAD signaling and regulatory strategies governing pathway activity show a wide range of variation across developmental and stem-cell systems. In the present review, we summarize insights from six major biological contexts-Drosophila embryo, germline stem cells, and the larval and pupal wing discs; the Danio rerio (
papers.summary: This review examines how the conserved BMP-SMAD signaling pathway operates across different animal species and tissues, highlighting that while the core signaling architecture is shared, the quantitative dynamics and regulatory strategies vary widely. It synthesizes findings from six major biological contexts, including Drosophila embryos and wing discs, germline stem cells, and zebrafish, to illustrate these differences.

papers.title: A genome-scale metabolic model of a pathosystem sheds light on bacterial wilt.
papers.abstract: During plant infection, complex metabolic interactions occur between the host and the pathogen, including direct competition for resources. While pathogens exploit host-derived nutrients to sustain growth and virulence, plants attempt to restrict pathogen proliferation by limiting nutrient availability. To quantify the contribution of these trophic interactions to disease development, we developed a mathematical model of plant-pathogen metabolism. A genome-scale metabolic model of the pathogen was integrated with a genome-scale, multiorgan metabolic model of the plant and calibrated using expe
papers.summary: This study presents a genome-scale metabolic model of a plant-pathogen pathosystem, integrating pathogen and multiorgan plant metabolism to quantify nutrient competition during bacterial wilt infection. The model, calibrated with experimental data, sheds light on how trophic interactions between host and pathogen contribute to disease development.

papers.title: Trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging for 13C-metabolic flux analysis: Evidence-based flux inference under structural model uncertainty.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of intracellular metabolic fluxes is central to systems biology and biotechnology. Flux estimation relies on biochemical network models, with 13C-metabolic flux analysis (MFA) being the state-of-the-art approach. However, isotope labeling data are often insufficient to uniquely support a single network formulation. In such cases, flux estimates become model-dependent, highlighting the need for methods that explicitly account for structural uncertainty. Bayesian model averaging provides a principled framework for this purpose, but its application to 13C-MFA has so far be
papers.summary: This paper introduces a trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging approach for 13C-metabolic flux analysis that explicitly accounts for structural uncertainty in metabolic network models. The method enables evidence-based flux inference when isotope labeling data cannot uniquely support a single network formulation, providing more robust flux estimates.

papers.title: Sex-aware causal inference assessment of the immune system in complex neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: Sex differences, in terms of prevalence, symptoms and disease progression, are established in the aetiology of complex neurodegenerative diseases, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease, but the underlying biology driving these differences remains poorly understood. There is emerging evidence from genetic and functional analyses affirming the role of the immune system in such diseases, but a thorough assessment of sex differences in the link between the immune system and neurodegenerative diseases remains lacking. Here, we applied a robust causal i
papers.summary: This study uses sex-aware causal inference methods to investigate the relationship between the immune system and complex neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS, Parkinson's, and Alzheimer's. It finds that immune-related genetic influences on these diseases differ between sexes, highlighting the importance of considering sex in causal analyses.

papers.title: WILDkCAT: extract, retrieve, and predict enzyme turnover numbers of constraint-based metabolic models.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme turnover numbers are essential for building enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models. However, collecting and curating these parameters remains a major bottleneck. Indeed, kcat values are scattered across multiple databases, reported under varying experimental conditions, and often missing for many enzymes. To address this challenge, we present WILDkCAT, a Python-based pipeline that enables the retrieval of kcat values from wild-type enzyme measured under user-specified pH and temperature ranges for a given metabolic model. The application to Escherichia coli (iML1515)
papers.summary: WILDkCAT is a Python pipeline that automatically retrieves enzyme turnover numbers (kcat values) for constraint-based metabolic models, filtering by user-specified pH and temperature conditions. It addresses the bottleneck of scattered and inconsistent kcat data by providing a streamlined extraction and prediction workflow, demonstrated on the E. coli model iML1515.

papers.title: Causal intervention validation of gene regulatory signals in scGPT.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models such as scGPT have been promoted as representations of gene regulation, but their advertised regulatory signal has been judged largely from attention weights, which are correlational. We ask a deliberately bounded question: whether direct interventions on scGPT gene tokens-causal with respect to the model's own computation-recover model-internal transcription-factor (TF)-target dependencies that align with curated references, whether that signal is robust, and whether it transfers to real perturbation responses. We separate these into two explicit validation axes
papers.summary: This paper tests whether scGPT, a single-cell foundation model, can recover gene regulatory relationships through direct causal interventions on its gene tokens, rather than relying on correlational attention weights. The authors find that these model-internal interventions do recover transcription factor-target dependencies that align with curated references, and they assess the robustness and transferability of this signal to real perturbation responses.

papers.title: Metabolic Modelling Facilitates the Design of Synthetic Communities by Simplifying Natural Microbial Communities.
papers.abstract: Natural microbial communities generally have complex compositions and unclear metabolic interactions, posing constraints on their applications. Clarifying these intricate interactions within microbial communities is challenging for traditional experiment-based methods. Here, we developed a simulation-based approach to design synthetic communities (SynComs) by simplifying complex microbial communities through metabolic modelling. We constructed genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) and curated them based on data obtained from straightforward experiments, ensuring these models precisely characte
papers.summary: This study presents a computational approach to design synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) by simplifying natural communities using genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs). The models are curated with experimental data to accurately represent metabolic interactions, enabling the prediction of simplified community compositions that retain key functions.

papers.title: CRITERIA: A network decomposition and elementary flux mode translation-based tool for computing equilibria of biochemical systems.
papers.abstract: Analytically deriving equilibria, which often govern the long-term behavior of biochemical reaction networks, is essential for understanding cellular decision-making and robustness, yet remains computationally challenging for large and complex systems. The COMPILES framework of Hernandez et al. addresses this problem via network decomposition but is limited by a computationally intensive translation step and by its restriction to networks with zero kinetic deficiency. We introduce CRITERIA (Computing paRametrized posITive EquilibRIA), a new framework that overcomes these limitations through tw
papers.summary: CRITERIA is a new computational tool that efficiently computes equilibria of biochemical reaction networks by decomposing the network and translating elementary flux modes, overcoming the computational bottlenecks and kinetic deficiency restrictions of the previous COMPILES framework. It enables analytical derivation of steady states for larger and more complex systems, which is crucial for understanding cellular decision-making and robustness.

papers.title: Urinary proteomic signature of exercise intolerance in patients at risk of heart failure: evidence from the HOMAGE trial.
papers.abstract: Urinary proteomic profiling (UPP) provides insights in disease mechanisms and origin of symptoms. Using UPP, this study aimed at deepening insight in the biology of exercise tolerance.
papers.summary: This study used urinary proteomic profiling to investigate the biological basis of exercise intolerance in patients at risk of heart failure, identifying a proteomic signature associated with reduced exercise capacity. The findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying exercise intolerance and may aid in risk stratification and personalized management.

papers.title: Aerobic conditioning and ginsenoside modulation modify molecular resilience in middle-aged rats: Differential effects of individual and combined interventions.
papers.abstract: Hippocampal aging is characterized by early cognitive decline, disrupted redox homeostasis, and shifts in amyloid processing. This study evaluated the modulatory effects of aerobic exercise and ginseng supplementation, both individually and concurrently, against these alterations. Middle-aged Wistar rats (n = 30) were allocated into young control, middle-aged control, exercise, ginseng supplementation, and combined intervention groups, and assessed through T-maze and Morris Water Maze tasks. Hippocampal integrity was examined with Cresyl violet staining and Nrf2 protein immunohistochemistry. G
papers.summary: This study in middle-aged rats found that aerobic exercise and ginseng supplementation, alone or combined, modulate molecular markers of hippocampal aging, including redox homeostasis and amyloid processing, with differential effects depending on the intervention. The combined intervention showed distinct benefits, suggesting potential for multi-modal strategies to support brain health in aging.

papers.title: Rhizospheric Microbes and Nanoparticles Synergize to Enhance Plant Immune Responses.
papers.abstract: Sustainable crop production increasingly requires innovative strategies that can enhance plant resilience while reducing dependence on synthetic agrochemicals. Recent advances in nanotechnology and rhizosphere microbiome research have created new opportunities to strengthen plant defense systems through integrated biological and material-based approaches. This review introduces the concept of nanobiotic synergies, defined as the strategic combination of engineered or biologically synthesized nanoparticles with beneficial rhizospheric microorganisms to improve plant immunity, stress tolerance,
papers.summary: This review introduces the concept of 'nanobiotic synergies,' where nanoparticles and beneficial rhizosphere microbes are combined to enhance plant immunity and stress tolerance, offering a sustainable alternative to synthetic agrochemicals. It highlights recent advances in nanotechnology and microbiome research that enable integrated biological and material-based strategies for crop protection.

papers.title: Metabolic Task Analysis Reveals Distinct Metabotypes in End-Stage Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is associated with shifts in cardiac metabolism. However, those shifts vary widely across patients, likely reflecting the diverse underlying causes of the disease. Identifying metabolic subtypes, or metabotypes, in DCM patients could help tailor treatments to patient needs. Hence, having a practical approach to identify these metabotypes would be a significant advance toward precision medicine in DCM.
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct metabolic subtypes (metabotypes) in end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy patients by analyzing cardiac metabolic tasks, revealing that metabolic shifts vary widely across patients. The findings suggest a practical approach for classifying patients into metabotypes, which could enable more tailored treatments and advance precision medicine for DCM.

papers.title: Testican-1-MMP axis in tumour extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling: interaction dynamics analysis and an in silico perspective.
papers.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a pivotal role in facilitating tumour development, invasiveness, metastasis, and immunoevasive processes through dynamic ECM remodelling processes. Testican-1 (SPOCK1), an excretory matricellular proteoglycan, is suggested to exert a role in the facilitation of ECM remodelling processes through interacting with matrix metalloproteases (MMPs) and even its less known forms. The structural mechanisms of interactions between testican-1 and MMPs were studied, and their roles in tumour-promotion pathway processes were also examined using a computational approach
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to analyze the structural interactions between Testican-1 (SPOCK1) and matrix metalloproteases (MMPs), revealing how these interactions may drive tumour extracellular matrix remodelling and promote cancer progression. The findings provide an in silico perspective on the Testican-1-MMP axis as a potential target in tumour biology.

papers.title: MultiCausGRN: directed prior-guided graph attention model for multi-omics gene regulatory network inference.
papers.abstract: Existing methods for gene regulatory network (GRN) inference rely primarily on gene expression data alone or on lower-resolution bulk sequencing data. Despite recent advances in integrating chromatin accessibility and RNA sequencing, inferring GRNs from paired single-cell multi-omics data remains challenging due to noise, sparsity, and complex nonlinear regulatory relationships.
papers.summary: MultiCausGRN is a new deep learning model that infers gene regulatory networks from paired single-cell multi-omics data (chromatin accessibility and gene expression) by using a directed prior-guided graph attention mechanism. It addresses challenges of noise, sparsity, and nonlinear regulatory relationships, improving GRN inference accuracy over existing methods.

papers.title: Integrative single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis identifies UBE2C+ proliferative tumor cells and immune-stromal regulatory crosstalk in small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive neuroendocrine malignancy characterized by rapid proliferation, early dissemination, and limited durable benefit from current chemoimmunotherapy. Although immune checkpoint blockade has modestly improved clinical outcomes, the regulatory logic linking malignant cell states to the tumor immune microenvironment remains incompletely understood. Here, we applied an integrative single-nucleus transcriptomic framework to dissect tumor cell heterogeneity, regulatory programs, and immune-stromal communication networks in SCLC.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative single-nucleus transcriptomics to characterize tumor heterogeneity and immune-stromal interactions in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), identifying a UBE2C+ proliferative tumor cell population and regulatory crosstalk networks. The findings provide new insights into how malignant cell states relate to the tumor microenvironment, potentially informing future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: NSFC-funded Chinese materia medica research (2015-2024): achievements output, research characteristics, and evolution.
papers.abstract: To systematically analyze the project completion status and research characteristics in the field of Chinese Materia Medica (CMM, discipline code H32) funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), thereby providing a basis for optimizing the allocation of scientific research resources and adjusting funding strategies.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes NSFC-funded projects in Chinese Materia Medica from 2015 to 2024, summarizing their output, research characteristics, and evolution. It provides insights into funding patterns and research trends, which could help optimize resource allocation and funding strategies in this field.

papers.title: A generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated XAI governance for cancer diagnostics: from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnostics is being reshaped by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, yet a persistent gap separates computational performance from clinical trust. Systematic reviews confirm that 83% of XAI studies in oncology excluded clinicians from development or evaluation, 87% lacked rigorous assessment of XAI explanations, and no universally accepted quality metrics for XAI outputs currently exist. Concurrently, generative AI (GenAI) is entering oncology at an unprecedented pace, yet it operates largely without formal interpretability governance.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a generative AI multi-agent framework for cancer diagnostics that integrates explainable AI (XAI) governance to bridge the gap between computational performance and clinical trust. It addresses the lack of clinician involvement and rigorous XAI evaluation in oncology by incorporating interpretability governance into the framework, aiming to improve both multi-omics interpretation and lifestyle risk stratification.

papers.title: Toward precision neuroscience in Alzheimer's disease: the role of multimodal AI.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly understood as a biologically defined and heterogeneous continuum, requiring models that move beyond symptom-based diagnosis toward individualized risk prediction, stratification, and intervention.
papers.summary: This review discusses how multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate diverse data types—such as genetics, neuroimaging, and biomarkers—to advance precision medicine in Alzheimer's disease. It highlights AI's potential for individualized risk prediction, patient stratification, and tailored interventions, moving beyond traditional symptom-based diagnosis.

papers.title: Platelet-rich plasma and folliculogenesis: a systematic mechanistic review and computational pathway analysis.
papers.abstract: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been proposed as a potential intervention for promoting ovarian follicular development. However, its underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether the mechanisms through which PRP may influence follicular development are consistent with previously established regulatory mechanisms of human folliculogenesis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and computational pathway analysis examines whether platelet-rich plasma (PRP) could promote ovarian follicular development through mechanisms consistent with known regulators of human folliculogenesis. The authors find that PRP's proposed effects align with established pathways, suggesting a plausible biological basis for its use in fertility treatments.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming orchestrates microglial fate in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury: a spatiotemporal immunometabolic perspective.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a critical pathological cascade that paradoxically exacerbates neurological damage following revascularization therapy for acute ischemic stroke (AIS). The pathogenesis of CIRI is intricately linked to dysregulated neuroinflammation, with microglia-the resident innate immune cells of the central nervous system-serving as central orchestrators of this response. Emerging evidence indicates that microglia undergo profound metabolic reprogramming encompassing glucose metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, fatty acid metabolism, and NA
papers.summary: This review discusses how metabolic reprogramming in microglia—including shifts in glucose, TCA cycle, and fatty acid metabolism—drives their pro- or anti-inflammatory states during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. It highlights a spatiotemporal immunometabolic perspective, suggesting that targeting microglial metabolism could offer new therapeutic strategies for stroke.

papers.title: Uncovering the molecular landscape of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer: A relieff-based feature selection analysis on RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Diffuse Gastric Cancer (DGC) is an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis and a lack of specific biomarkers, representing a critical unmet need in oncology. This study aimed to elucidate the key molecular drivers of DGC by integrating RNA-seq data with a multi-faceted bioinformatics approach.
papers.summary: This study uses a ReliefF-based feature selection method on RNA-seq data to identify key molecular drivers of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer (DGC), a subtype with poor prognosis and few biomarkers. The approach highlights potential gene signatures that could serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets, addressing an unmet clinical need.

papers.title: Integrative precision oncology in neuroblastoma: multi-omics biomarkers, molecular targets, and immunotherapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most frequent extracranial solid tumor of young children and demonstrates a wide range of biological behavior, from spontaneous regression to highly aggressive metastatic disease. Recent advances in genomics, epigenetics, tumor microenvironment biology, and multi-omics technologies have greatly enhanced understanding of neuroblastoma pathogenesis and enabled the development of precision diagnostic and prognostic approaches. This review examines current evidence for molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neuroblastoma initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistanc
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics findings in neuroblastoma, highlighting how genomic, epigenetic, and tumor microenvironment studies have improved understanding of disease pathogenesis and enabled precision diagnostic and prognostic approaches. It also discusses molecular targets and immunotherapeutic strategies, emphasizing the potential for integrating these biomarkers into clinical management.

papers.title: A systems biology approach to find representative genes in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.abstract: In this study, we modeled gene expression profile data from Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) and healthy cases. At first, the GEO-GSE9476 dataset was processed, and a total of 341 genes were identified as differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in patients, and 599 DEGs in healthy individuals. Gene Ontology and pathway analysis on DEGs led to the identification of 5 Transcription Factors for patients and 3 for healthy cases. Analysis of the respective metabolic pathways revealed a common region in the metabolic pathway between AML and Tuberculosis (TB) that confirmed the validity of our procedure du
papers.summary: This study uses a systems biology approach to analyze gene expression data from AML patients and healthy individuals, identifying differentially expressed genes and transcription factors. The authors found a shared metabolic pathway region between AML and Tuberculosis, which validates their analytical method and may reveal common disease mechanisms.
